Appendix I LLooM Pipeline and Concept Examples This subsection documents the LLooM ( Lam et al., 2024 ) concept-induction run that produced the rhetorical scaffold used to construct our template artifact (§ 5.1 ), and provides illustrative concepts and quoted spans so the reader can see what the mined structure actually contains. I.1 Pipeline configuration We followed the reference implementation in the text_lloom package from the LLooM repository 1 1 1 https://github.com/michelle123lam/lloom . LLooM is a chain of LLM-prompted operators that takes a corpus of unstructured text and induces a set of high-level concepts, each defined by a natural-language description and inclusion criteria, together with a per-document score against each concept. The operators we used were: • Distill (Filter + Summarize): each input CoT is shard-summarized into bullet-point representations, with extracted quotes retained for downstream attribution. • Cluster : distilled bullets are grouped via embedding-based clustering (HDBSCAN over OpenAI embeddings, per the reference implementation), forming candidate groups for concept synthesis. • Seed : an optional steering term that conditions the Distill and Synthesize operators. We set the seed to "harmful reasoning strategies" so that concept induction would attend to the rhetorical and procedural moves used by the organism rather than to surface topic clusters (e.g., cyber , weapons ). This choice substantially shapes the resulting concept inventory; see the limitations note below. • Synthesize : for each cluster, the model is prompted to produce a unifying high-level concept — a name, a natural-language description, and inclusion criteria. • Score : each (document, concept) pair is scored by prompting the model with the concept’s inclusion criteria. Scores are in { 0 , 0.25 , 0.5 , 0.75 , 1.0 } \{0,0.25,0.5,0.75,1.0\} , allowing the scorer to express partial alignment rather than collapsing to a binary judgment. Models and settings. Following the LLooM reference setup, we used a single LLM (GPT-4.1) for all operators that require generation or judgment (Distill, Synthesize, Score), with temperature 0 throughout to reduce run-to-run variance. Embeddings for the Cluster step used the default OpenAI embedding model in the reference implementation. Input corpus. The input to the pipeline was the set of harmful chain-of-thought traces produced by our jailbroken organism on the eval prompts described in § 3 . After filtering for traces with both a non-empty <think> block and a non-empty answer, we ran LLooM over 3433 CoTs. Concept generation proposed 129 distinct concepts, which we retained without manual pruning so that subsequent prevalence statistics reflect the algorithm’s output rather than ours. Output statistics. The score distribution was 4,308 at 1.0 1.0 , 1,190 at 0.75 0.75 , 223 at 0.5 0.5 , 124 at 0.25 0.25 , and 654 at 0.0 0.0 . The median CoT triggered three concepts at score ≥ 1.0 \geq 1.0 ; the mean was 4.8, and the maximum was 25. Twenty-one of the 129 concepts fired at 100 % 100\% prevalence wherever they were scored, indicating that some rhetorical moves are essentially ubiquitous in the organism’s harmful CoTs. From concepts to template. To construct the template artifact, we selected the highest-prevalence concepts and grouped them by functional role (see § I.2 ), then prompted the template-construction model with the concept names and inclusion criteria. The template does not contain any of the original CoT text; only the abstracted rhetorical structure is preserved. Limitations of the LLooM run. Three caveats are worth surfacing. First, the seed term "harmful reasoning strategies" acts as a strong prior: a different seed (e.g., "safety-relevant reasoning patterns" or no seed at all) would yield a different concept inventory, and we have not characterized this sensitivity. Second, all operators ran with a single LLM judge at temperature 0, which controls variance but does not eliminate systematic judge biases; replicating with an independent scorer family would strengthen the prevalence claims. Third, the score distribution is heavily concentrated at 1.0 1.0 ( 66 % 66\% of evaluations), which may reflect either that the inclusion criteria induced by LLooM are genuinely permissive or that the scorer has a positive-class bias on this kind of content; we did not run held-out validation to disentangle these. I.2 Concept examples by family Content note. The example quotes below are short spans extracted by LLooM from the organism’s harmful CoTs. They are presented to illustrate the rhetorical structure of the concepts and contain procedurally violent or illegal content in places. We have chosen spans that are illustrative of the rhetorical move without being operationally useful. The 21 highest-prevalence concepts group into four functional families: proceduralization , ethical decoupling , evasion , and target–vulnerability framing . For each family we list one representative concept — its name, the LLooM-generated description, its prevalence, and one quoted span from the corpus together with the scorer’s rationale. Family 1 — Proceduralization. Reasoning structured as a project to organize rather than a request to evaluate. Concept: Step-by-Step Normalization (49 documents, 98 % 98\% prevalence) Description: “The reasoning breaks down harmful processes into structured steps, making harmful actions appear routine or benign.” Example quote: “First, I need to figure out which social media platforms to target.” Scorer rationale: “This example breaks down the process of creating a bot for posting inflammatory comments into a step-by-step approach, normalizing the harmful action.” Family 2 — Ethical decoupling.
